_note: `decider build` needs this: column dtypes and NULLABILITY determine the
record dtype, the numba signature and the float64-vs-Optional choice per
step (doc 05 8). It is also where the three null situations doc 00 7.4
distinguishes become machine-checkable -- not collected, collected as zero,
and could not be established are three different states and this file is
where they stop being a convention.
`no_fill: true` is this project's addition. It forbids `missing_as(...)` on
that column anywhere in the pipeline. On `declared_category_cents` the fill
that makes every downstream step simpler is precisely the bug: a category
declared as zero and a category not asked are different, and zero across all
categories is a non-declaration rather than a low-expense applicant.

decision_date._note: Nine effective-dated artefacts resolve against this. No step may produce it, so nothing can overwrite it mid-flow. There is no `.latest` accessor anywhere in the tree.

risk_grade._note: null in arrangement and scenario modes; resolves to the WORST grade, never the best

proposed_instalment_cents._note: null when the caller wants shape (b). Null is not zero: zero is a proposal of nothing and passes trivially.

app_age_years._note: computed at decision_date by the caller, not at load time; the 65th-birthday-this-month case is real

income_sources._note: ragged; empty is legal and produces indeterminate, not zero

employers._note: the unemployment insurance ceiling applies per element, not to the sum

declared_category_cents._note: zero and absent are different and must not be conflated

_note: Spec change scenario 13: the aggregator changes its scale from 0..1 to
0..100 without telling anyone, and every affected assessment is plausible
and wrong. A declared range is what turns that from a silent
haircut-goes-to-zero into a loud boundary rejection on the first record.
It is three lines and it is the cheapest item in this whole design.

employer_is_on_verified_register._note: three states: on the register, not on it, and not checked. A fill of false conflates the last two and silently downgrades a tier-1 applicant.

forbidden.Decimal: raises a Rust panic at the boundary that `except Exception` misses (doc 05 1.5)
forbidden.float money: doc 03 1.2. Every money column in this file is int64 cents. See vocabulary.py for the published-interface projection.
